title: Claudia Sheinbaum Announces Cancellation of La Parota Dam in Guerrero; Water Wells Will Be Built Instead
author: Redacción/SinEmbargo
content:
_This article by the SinEmbargo newsroom originally appeared in the[July 26,
2026 edition of SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4844264/csp-anuncia-
cancelacion-de-presa-la-parota-en-guerrero-mejor-se-haran-pozos-de-agua/),
published with the express authorization of El Sur._

**Acapulco, July 26 (El Sur).—** President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo announced
this Sunday that the federal government canceled the**La Parota dam project**
, in the rural area of Acapulco, Guerrero, because of the impact it would have
caused on the communities, and noted that, in its place, wells are being built
to supply water to the port.

At a public event in Ciudad Renacimiento, in the upper coastal area, the
federal leader said she communicated the decision on Saturday to the residents
of the rural area.

> "I informed all of rural Acapulco that the La Parota dam project is
> canceled. We are no longer going to do it because it greatly affected the
> community," she stated.

Sheinbaum's announcement implies recognition of the social protest that arose
two decades ago against the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) project in
the bed of the Papagayo River, about 30 kilometers (km) from Acapulco.

> Supervisamos la obra de los nuevos pozos radiales que contribuirán a
> fortalecer el abastecimiento de agua para Acapulco. Cada avance representa
> un paso más para el bienestar.  
> Gracias por su cálido recibimiento, su confianza y su cariño. Ese amor es
> correspondido y nos motiva a…
> [pic.twitter.com/UiusbIcTbo](https://t.co/UiusbIcTbo)
>
> -- Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) [July 26,
> 2026](https://x.com/Claudiashein/status/2081411756035866736?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

In explaining the decision, the head of the Executive branch noted that the
federal government is already carrying out works to strengthen the water
supply in Acapulco, which will replace the hydroelectric project.

She also detailed that in the area where the dam was to be built, radial wells
and elevated tanks are being developed that will allow water to be distributed
by gravity to different neighborhoods of the port.

> "In substitution for that project, we are building these wells to be able to
> bring water to Acapulco," she stated. "It is pumped to the upper part and
> the water reaches the different neighborhoods," she added.

Likewise, she recalled that, after the passage of hurricanes "Otis" and
"John," the pumps that captured water from the Papagayo River were damaged, so
new infrastructure is now being built to prevent a similar situation from
occurring again during the river's floods.

> "We are doing sanitation works so there is no contamination of the rivers,
> and dredging so they have enough space and do not overflow in case of an
> abnormal situation. Knock on wood!" she expressed.

Finally, she said that the drinking water networks in the neighborhoods of the
upper part of Acapulco will also be renewed, beginning with Ciudad
Renacimiento.

![Members of the CETEG teachers' union hold a banner during President
Sheinbaum's visit to Acapulco](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/2026-07-26-parota-dam-canceled-02-ceteg.jpg)Photo: El
Sur

Members of the State Coordinating Committee of Education Workers in Guerrero
(CETEG) also presented a list of demands to President Sheinbaum Pardo today
during her second day of a work tour in Acapulco.

A brief encounter between CETEG members and the federal leader took place as
the head of the Executive branch was arriving in her vehicle at the facilities
of the Ciudad Renacimiento Sports Center.

The general secretary of the CETEG, Elvira Veleces Morales, approached the
truck and handed President Sheinbaum Pardo a document with the union's
demands, among them the repeal of the Law of the Institute for Social Security
and Services for State Workers (ISSSTE), an increase to the Teacher's Day
bonus, and recategorization.

Veleces Morales briefly explained the demands. The President did not get out
of the vehicle and merely signed to acknowledge receipt of the document.

The Guerrero leader said that "wherever the President appears," they will be
there to present their union demands to her.
